summary.answer:
A1 (basically Florida) is a dense customer cluster, but customers there behave the same as everywhere else in the US.

**Size**
- **1,739 US customers** fall inside A1, which is **7.8%** of the 22,360 US users. That's slightly more than Florida's share of the US population (about 6.6%, a general figure, not from this data).
- The dark hexagons are along both coasts and the I‑4 corridor. Jacksonville has the most customers (83), followed by Miami (52), Orlando (49), Cape Coral (36), Tampa (33), Port St. Lucie (28) and Tallahassee (27). The Miami metro (Miramar, Hialeah) adds about 50 more.
- The interior and Big Bend are sparse, which matches where people actually live.

**Behaviour compared with the rest of the US**
| | A1 | Rest of US |
|---|---|---|
| Share of users who have ordered | 79.9% | 80.3% |
| Revenue per user | $110 | $109 |
| Items returned or cancelled | 23.7% | 24.7% |
| Average age / share female | 41.3 / 51% | 41.1 / 50% |
| Users who came from Search | 71% | 71% |

There's nothing unusual here. The cluster just reflects where people live. Florida customers buy and return at the same rates as everyone else, and their returns are about 1 point lower.

**The one real gap is shipping distance.** No distribution centre is in Florida. The closest are Savannah, GA (about 415 km from Orlando, and further from Miami), Charleston (521 km) and Mobile (687 km). About 1,700 customers is a lot of demand to serve from out of state. If delivery speed or shipping cost matters, south and central Florida is worth a look.

Map annotations marked by the user (refer to them by id; WKT is lon lat, use ST_GEOGFROMTEXT(wkt) in BigQuery; get_annotations returns GeoJSON for map layers):
- A1: Polygon, bbox [-87.6, 24.9, -79.8, 31], ~198,756 km²

Attached: a screenshot of the map as the user sees it, with the marked area(s) labelled by id.

input.sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((-87.6 31, -86.2 30.9, -85 31, -83.6 30.9, -82.3 30.8, -81.3 30.9, -80.9 30, -80.5 28.9, -80 27.6, -79.8 26.4, -80 25.3, -80.6 24.9, -81.4 25.2, -81.9 26, -82.6 27, -82.9 28.1, -83 29, -83.9 29.8, -85.2 29.5, -86.4 30.2, -87.6 30.2, -87.6 31))') g),
u AS (SELECT u.*, ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude,latitude),(SELECT g FROM a)) inA FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u WHERE country='United States'),
oi AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) o, SUM(sale_price) rev, COUNTIF(status IN ('Returned','Cancelled')) bad, COUNT(*) items FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` GROUP BY 1)
SELECT inA, COUNT(*) users, COUNTIF(oi.user_id IS NOT NULL) buyers, SUM(o) orders, ROUND(SUM(rev)) rev, ROUND(SUM(rev)/COUNT(*),1) rev_per_user, ROUND(SUM(bad)/SUM(items),3) bad_rate, ROUND(AVG(age),1) age, ROUND(COUNTIF(gender='F')/COUNT(*),3) female, ROUND(COUNTIF(traffic_source='Search')/COUNT(*),3) search
FROM u LEFT JOIN oi ON oi.user_id=u.id GROUP BY 1
